ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Sick Visit — George Washington — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for fever, cough and chest pain

text.paragraph: Fever, cough and right-sided chest pain for a day, after a cold. [S]

Mr. Washington asked for a same-day visit. Two days ago he had a sore throat and a runny nose. Since yesterday afternoon he has had chills, a fever of 38.6 °C at home, a cough bringing up rust-colored sputum, a sharp pain in the right lower chest on deep breaths, and breathlessness on the stairs. He is drinking and eating soft food. He has no confusion, no vomiting, and no difficulty swallowing or swelling in the throat or neck. Two lower implants were placed seven weeks ago and the sites are comfortable. He had a single preoperative dose of amoxicillin then, but no other antibiotic, hospital stay or intravenous treatment in the past three months. He has no heart, lung, liver or kidney disease, diabetes or immune problem, and has never smoked. He had the pneumococcal vaccine eight weeks ago and the influenza vaccine in the autumn. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1790-05-11; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired but alert and speaking in full sentences; temperature 38.4 °C, pulse 98, respiratory rate 20, blood pressure 118/72, oxygen saturation 95% on room air
Pharynx mildly red without swelling; voice normal; implant sites closed and healthy under the soft-lined lower denture
Supple; no tender nodes or swelling
Crackles and bronchial breath sounds at the right base; no wheeze
Pain and difficulty chewing and speaking with loose, worn complete dentures that click and move; cause and treatment under evaluation with prosthodontics
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented painful dentures; superseded when the consultation made the diagnosis.

Complete edentulism of both jaws (American College of Prosthodontists diagnostic index class III: mandibular bone height about 14 mm, a flat lower ridge, a high muscle attachment), with complete dentures more than eight years old that no longer fit; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented tooth loss from his twenties and his full dentures
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the prosthodontic consultation; the cause is recorded as unspecified because the sources do not establish why his teeth were lost.

Two shallow ulcers under the lower denture flange, probably traumatic from an ill-fitting denture, with no induration, red or white patch, or neck lymph node; to be re-examined two weeks after the denture is left out between meals
S — Synthetic oral finding at intake; healed by the consultation, which confirmed denture-related traumatic ulcers.
Unintended weight loss of about 5.6 kg (6%) over six months from a narrowed, soft diet; at risk of malnutrition (MNA-SF 10)
S — Synthetic nutrition problem linked to the documented difficulty eating with dentures.
Community-acquired pneumonia of the right lower lobe, CURB-65 0, treated as an outpatient; seven weeks after lower implants were placed; resolved
S — Synthetic acute illness echoing, in much milder form, his documented pneumonia of May 1790; not a claim about its cause.

list.item:
Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe (J18.9). Pneumonia confirmed on the chest radiograph. CURB-65 0: no confusion, urea nitrogen 16 mg/dL (below 20), respiratory rate 20, blood pressure 118/72, age under 65; oxygen saturation 95%, so outpatient treatment is appropriate. White cell count 13.2. Rapid SARS-CoV-2 and influenza tests negative. As an adult without comorbidities, he is treated with high-dose amoxicillin; the single preoperative dose seven weeks ago does not change the choice. Sputum and blood cultures and procalcitonin are not needed for outpatient pneumonia. No sign of an upper-airway infection. [S]
Amoxicillin 1 g three times daily for five days.
Acetaminophen for fever, fluids and rest; time off work for several days.
Clean the dentures and implant sites as usual and keep the dentures out overnight.
A phone check in 48 hours; return at once for breathlessness at rest, confusion, oxygen saturation below 92% if checked at home, chest pain that worsens, or no improvement in 72 hours.
Clinical resolution review in two weeks; no routine follow-up chest radiograph if he recovers.

Complete edentulism with implants healing (K08.103). Implant sites healthy; no interaction between the pneumonia treatment and the implant plan. [S]
Attachment connection stays planned for about three months after implant placement.

Follow-up: Phone check in 48 hours. Clinical resolution review in two weeks. Return sooner as above. Next scheduled visit 1790-05-25: clinical resolution review two weeks after outpatient pneumonia, with the implant healing and weight. [S]
